title: The Down Beat club, Rainbow Grill and the stranger from Denmark
summary: Ann and he scrape through before a good Down Beat job and a band at the top of Rockefeller Center, then a bearded visitor appears.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That's when you really started what became your really big thing in Europe lateron.
Travelling around withyour trumpet and your suitcase and your wife---

Yeah. And, uh, that all started-- well, I kicked through that period of time and survived it and I must say that Ann and I had some real tough times paying our bills on a few occasions but, then, it started to pick up a little and then I worked the Down Beat, [club] you know - in New York - and it was a nice paying job - and it had a nice band and, then, of course - toward the end of that scuffling around; I had the band in the 65 stories above the street in the---
No, the Rainbow Grill is not in the Waldorf Astoria---
There's two rooms up there; there's a room up there - the Rainbow Grill - is that it?
And, then, the big room -- I played in the big room. And, I played the time when they had all New Orleans food and all this and I had a wonderful band up there.
That's that poster we got up on the wall.

Yeah and I played up there for --- and they loved our band and wanted us to come back but there's the time - right there - I had played the New York Jazz Festival at that particular point; I wish I could think of the year.
It could be. Anyway, a very strange fellow came to see me one night with a long beard and long hair and a funny overcoat---
Well, you were getting into the European thing now---
